# Welcome {.unnumbered}

These notes accompany **BIOL 7950: Bayesian Inference for Biologists** at Kennesaw State University.

The goal of this course is to introduce Bayesian statistical thinking and modern Bayesian analysis for biological data.

## Course organization

The book is organized into three parts:

1. Foundations: introduces the basic ideas behind Bayesian inference, Bayes' rule, and how Bayesian inference differs from frequentist inference. Also introduces some key aspects of working with Bayesian models in R and JAGS.
1. Bayesian analyses in R and JAGS: demonstrates Bayesian versions of common models for biology like linear models, GLMs, and nonlinear models.
1. Special applications: demonstrates some situations where Bayesian methods really shine, like mark-recapture and state space models.

## Suggested reading

There is no required textbook for this course, but if you want a book to help you on your Bayesian journey you could do worse than the following:

Albert J. 2009. Bayesian computation with R. Springer Science+Business Media, New York. *Unlike most books on this list, this book focuses on implementing Bayesian methods in R itself. The mathematical exposition is a bit dense but was helpful for understanding exactly how MCMC relates to inference.*

Gelman A, Carlin JB, Stern HS, Rubin DB. 2013. Bayesian data analysis. 3rd edition. Taylor & Francis Group, Boca Raton, Florida, USA. *The all-time classic, written by some of the biggest names in modern Bayesian theory.*

Kéry M. 2010. Introduction to WinBUGS for Ecologists. Academic Press, Burlington, Massachusetts, USA. *This was my first Bayesian book, and I can't recommend it highly enough. It explains the basics of Bayesian inference, WinBUGS, and how to implement some common statistical models ranging from t-tests to ANCOVA. Even if you are not an ecologist, the exposition and example code in this book are clear and easy to follow.*

Kéry M, Kellner KF. 2024. Applied Statistical Modelling for Ecologists. Academic Press, Burlington, Massachusetts, USA. *I just learned about this (August 2026) and will be buying it soon. If it is as good as the other books in the series, it'll go into my regular rotation.*

McCarthy MA. 2007. Bayesian methods for ecology. Cambridge University Press, New York. *Another WinBUGS-focused book, this is a nice complement to Kéry (2010) with a bit more theory. Even if you are not an ecologist, the exposition and example code in this book are clear and easy to follow.*
